name: @reactunity/scripts
description: Configuration and scripts for React Unity.
//webpack-dev-server: Deliberately held at 5.x. Version 6 moves to Express 5, whose path-to-regexp rewrite rejects the route patterns the react-dev-utils middlewares this dev server is built on still use (evalSourceMapMiddleware, redirectServedPathMiddleware, noopServiceWorkerMiddleware -- see config/webpackDevServer.config.js). react-dev-utils is unmaintained (12.0.1, 2022), so moving to 6 means replacing those middlewares, not bumping a version. Symptom if you try it: `react-unity-scripts start` prints "Starting the development server..." and hangs with nothing listening.
//@babel/core: Deliberately held at 7.x. babel-preset-react-app 10 -- the preset this whole pipeline compiles with -- peer-depends on @babel/core ^7, and Babel 8 requires every plugin and preset in the tree to be 8-compatible. Upgrading means replacing babel-preset-react-app first.
//typescript: Held at 6.x while the root and packages/create are on 7, and the peer range below caps consumers at <7 for the same reason: this package resolves the TypeScript *module* at three points -- config/modules.js, config/webpack.config.js (as fork-ts-checker's `typescriptPath`) and scripts/utils/verifyTypeScriptSetup.js -- all via `resolve.sync('typescript')`. TypeScript 7 publishes no CJS entry for `.` (its export map points at lib/version.cjs), and `resolve` reads `main`, not `exports`, so that call throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND and `react-unity-scripts` cannot start at all. Unblocking this means teaching fork-ts-checker about the native compiler, not bumping a range.
